derivation: Written by applying contract/semantics.md to the recorded frames by hand.
NOT generated by running any binding.
ts_str '2026-04/20-13:30:00' read as America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4 on that
date) gives 2026-04-20T17:30:00Z. The DLL's own ts_utc carries
5m/15m/30m/1h — the intraday grid runs from 09:30 ET. 17:30:00Z is
13:30 ET, which is 240 minutes after the 09:30 anchor; 240 divides by
5, 15, 30 and 60, so the instant is already a grid edge in all four.
1d — the daily grid anchors at 04:00 ET (§4). 13:30 ET is after 04:00,
publisher's timestamp is NOT the bucket: EL stamps a daily bar with
the chart's own Date/Time, and it is the binding that aligns.
notes: This fixture is the end-to-end coverage for wire v3's whole point — the
BarType/BarInterval → tf mapping in the DLL's wire_timeframe(). Before it
existed every recorded frame was tf '1m', so a regression in that table
(BarInterval 60 mapped to '60m', say) reached a binding with nothing in
CI to catch it, and a second binding had no sample to check against.
The QQQ frame comes from EL_PublishTickEx, the frozen legacy entry point.
It has no BarType/BarInterval parameters, so it can only ever have meant
1m — pinned here so the shim cannot drift.
TWO FRAMES ARE ABSENT ON PURPOSE. The harness also called EL_PublishBar
returned -5 and published nothing, which is why this fixture has 6 lines
and not 8. The DLL does not guess: an unmappable interval filed under a
default would put one interval's bars in another's partition, and nothing
seq is per-symbol (§6.1): SPY runs 1..5 across five different timeframes
